clue.text: Drunk bloated with the set meal

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A swollen drunk sits down to a fixed-price dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A table d'hote is a restaurant menu of fixed courses at a fixed price, unlike ordering a la carte.

clue.text: Speaker's changed course for savoir-faire

indicators.note: what a speaker says is heard rather than read, so the sound of the phrase counts, not its spelling

blocks.note: a sailing boat that has tacked has changed course against the wind

explanation.surface: A lecturer's change of direction is put down to social polish.
explanation.definitionFit: Savoir-faire is the knack of handling people gracefully, which is close to diplomacy and discretion.

clue.text: Very naughty boy born our absurdly High King

indicators.note: something done absurdly makes no sense, so the word before it is jumbled

blocks.note: in Monty Python's Life of Brian, Brian's mother insists he is not the Messiah but a very naughty boy
b. is the abbreviation for born
the letters of our rearranged

explanation.surface: A notorious rascal is born, absurdly, to rule as our supreme monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The Monty Python line is the key: 'He's not the Messiah, he's a very naughty boy!'
explanation.definitionFit: Brian Boru was the tenth-century Irish ruler who held the title of Ard Ri, overlord of all Ireland.

clue.text: Arden perhaps a person turning on house of God

indicators.note: turning round makes the word face the other way, so it is read from right to left

blocks.note: one = a person, as in 'one never knows'
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone spins round on a church, perhaps a forest-dweller from Arden.
explanation.walkthrough: Enoch Arden is Tennyson's poem about a shipwrecked sailor; Arden is the surname, the answer his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's sailor Enoch Arden is one man with that given name, so the surname serves as an example.

clue.text: Fault in fastening black paint applicator?

definitions.note: a painter applies paint, so a whimsical description of an artist

indicators.note: fastening means holding something firmly within, so one piece is wrapped round the other

blocks.note: a fault in an argument is a hole in it
B is the pencil abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A defect in the clasp of a black brush, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Hans Holbein the Younger was the Tudor court painter; the question mark flags the jokey definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Holbein was a German-born portraitist, and any artist working in oils is literally someone who puts colour on canvas.

clue.text: Child small goddess consumes in As You Like It

indicators.note: what consumes something takes it inside, so the goddess goes round the small letter

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A little one watches a tiny goddess eat during a performance of Shakespeare's comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's title is borrowed as a phrase: seasoning added according to your liking.
explanation.definitionFit: Recipes say add salt to taste, meaning in whatever amount pleases the cook, just as one likes.

clue.text: Unrecognised threat – composer fleeced?

blocks.note: Hugo Wolf was an Austrian composer of songs
fleeced read literally means wearing a fleece, the woolly coat of the flock

explanation.surface: A musician who has been swindled turns out to be a hidden danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleeced' looks like cheated, but here it means dressed in wool.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase from Aesop and the Gospels describes an enemy disguised as harmless, a danger nobody spots.

clue.text: Decorative feature of small book with doubled ring binding

indicators.note: binding wraps round and holds, so the doubled ring encloses the book

blocks.note: a ring is the round letter O, taken twice
vol. is the short form of volume

explanation.surface: An ornamental detail on a pocket book with a double-ring binder.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovolo is a convex quarter-round moulding used to ornament cornices and furniture in classical architecture.

clue.text: No real force set out at night

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the thing that is put out overnight

blocks.note: what is not real is false
a law with teeth has force behind it

explanation.surface: No genuine army is deployed under cover of darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' is the dentist's word for a full plate of dentures, put in a glass by the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentures are usually removed before sleep and left in a glass by the bedside until morning.

clue.text: See 6
Poisonous gas swamping breathable ones in city

indicators.note: swamping means engulfing, so the gas surrounds what follows

blocks.note: CO is the chemical formula for carbon monoxide
the gases one can breathe make up the atmosphere around us

explanation.surface: Toxic fumes overwhelm the clean atmosphere in an urban centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairo is the capital of Egypt, the largest urban centre on the Nile.

clue.text: Flyer unusually low after drop

indicators.note: done unusually means not in the normal way, so the next word is rearranged
after says the reworked word comes behind the other piece, though the clue prints it first

blocks.note: a drop of milk is a little
the three letters of low reshuffled

explanation.surface: A pilot flies strangely close to the ground after a sudden descent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the drop first even though it comes last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The little owl is a small European bird of prey, and any bird is a creature of the air.

clue.text: See 6
Some irony perhaps from tense painter

blocks.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
a painter is a rope tied to a boat's bow for mooring

explanation.surface: A nervous artist produces a touch of sarcasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painter' looks like an artist, but here it is the sailor's mooring line.
explanation.definitionFit: Irony is one figure of speech among many, alongside metaphor and hyperbole, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: See north captured by wee Scotsman, an ancient citizen

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor, so the first pieces go within the later ones

blocks.note: baby as an adjective means very small
lo is an old word for look or see
N is the compass abbreviation
Ian is the Scottish form of John, the stock crossword Scot

explanation.surface: Look north, where a small Scot has seized a resident of an old city.
explanation.definitionFit: Babylon was the great Mesopotamian capital, and its inhabitants lived there thousands of years ago.

clue.text: Greek cop regularly foresaw retreating

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
retreating means going backwards, so the assembled letters are read right to left

blocks.note: to cop or nail someone is to catch them
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A policeman from Athens saw it coming and backed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cop' reads as a police officer, but it is the verb to catch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aeolians were one of the main tribal divisions of the ancient Hellenes, settling Lesbos and Boeotia.

clue.text: On Tyneside perhaps look after labyrinth

blocks.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE
to rear a child is to look after it

explanation.surface: Someone in Newcastle is asked to care for a maze.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the Newcastle area in north-east England, so being on it puts you in NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomists call the cochlea and semicircular canals the labyrinth because of their winding passages.

clue.text: Unisex one-piece, not old, needing repair

indicators.note: not here means without, so a letter is taken away
something needing repair is broken, so its letters must be put back together differently

blocks.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A shabby swimsuit for either sex, not vintage, is in need of mending.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicene means having characteristics of both sexes or neither, so it covers clothing worn by anyone.

clue.text: Make sexy ones depraved coterie receives

indicators.note: depraved means corrupted, so the next word's letters are twisted
what receives something takes it inside, so the jumbled group holds the other piece

blocks.note: the letters of coterie rearranged
I is one, so ones in the plural are I's

explanation.surface: A debauched clique welcomes newcomers and spices things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To eroticise something is to give it a sexual character or charge.

clue.text: See 24
With desires, a threesome led by Hecate?

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
an itch is a craving

explanation.surface: Lustful urges hint at a three-in-a-bed arrangement led by a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: In Macbeth the three Weird Sisters answer to Hecate, goddess of witchcraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's trio of hags in Macbeth are scolded by their mistress Hecate in Act 3.

clue.text: Plant fruit with reduced value

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a fig is a fruit
worth is value

explanation.surface: A cheap shrub sold with some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Figwort is a herbaceous plant of the genus Scrophularia, once used against scrofula.

clue.text: Maybe slip up on supporting contenders

blocks.note: the field is all the runners in a race
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A runner may stumble while carrying the other competitors.
explanation.walkthrough: Slip is a cricket position beside the wicketkeeper, so a player standing there is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, slip is one of the close catching positions taken by a member of the fielding side.

clue.text: Single run stopped by wicket keeper

indicators.note: something stopped by an obstacle has it lodged in its path, so a letter goes inside

blocks.note: single = one
W is the cricket scorebook abbreviation
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A batsman's quick single is cut short by the wicketkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicket keeper' reads as one cricket position, but the definition is only the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps something possesses it, so a keeper is a holder or proprietor.

clue.text: This nation and Serbia might be inseparable

indicators.note: might be suggests the two names together could be rearranged into the final word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The answer plus SERBIA is an anagram of INSEPARABLE, so removing SERBIA's letters leaves the answer jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a Himalayan kingdom turned republic between India and China, so it is a country.

clue.text: Wicked solvers in Kent who'd worked out something better?

blocks.note: Old Nick is called the Wicked One
the setter addresses the solver as you
kent is Scots for knew; those in the ken, who've worked it out, are in the know

explanation.surface: Mischievous puzzlers in the Garden of England who cracked it, perhaps to good effect.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb runs: better the devil you know than the devil you don't, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says a familiar evil is preferable to an unknown one, so it is the better choice.

clue.text: Pear, peeled by cardinal, devoured

indicators.note: fruit that is peeled loses its skin, so the outside letters go and the middle stays

blocks.note: the inner two letters
ten is a cardinal number

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman, but it means a counting number.

clue.text: Once appropriate gathering prior to hunt

blocks.note: first meaning: an archaic adjective meaning fitting or proper
second meaning: the assembly of riders and hounds before a fox hunt

explanation.surface: A once-fitting assembly before riders set off after the fox.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adjective means suitable, as in 'it is meet and right', and the noun is the hunt's assembly.

clue.text: Found fault with force, endlessly hurt

indicators.note: endlessly means without an ending, so the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: to impel is to force
ached = hurt

explanation.surface: Someone was criticised for using force that caused endless pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach a statement or witness is to challenge its credibility, to call it into question.

taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: To twine is to twist or coil round something, as a creeper does round a post.

blocks.note: spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A river's tide falls away at evenly spaced moments.

clue.text: Styptic collar a temporary splint secures
